histogram.heading: Probability by basis state

caption.complete_one: {{occupied}} of {{total}} basis states has a non-zero probability, and it is drawn.
caption.complete_other: {{occupied}} of {{total}} basis states have a non-zero probability, and every one of them is drawn.
caption.capped_one: {{occupied}} of {{total}} basis states have a non-zero probability. The {{shown}} most probable are drawn one by one; the other one holds {{share}} and shares the last bar.
caption.capped_other: {{occupied}} of {{total}} basis states have a non-zero probability. The {{shown}} most probable are drawn one by one; the other {{hidden}} hold {{share}} between them and share the last bar.

histogram.phasorNote: Each arrow points along the phase of its amplitude, and its colour is that same angle. Two arrows pointing opposite ways are two paths cancelling.

counts.heading: Measured counts
counts.intro_one: This circuit measures before it ends, so it has no single final state. It was run {{shots}} times, and the classical register read the same value every time.
counts.intro_other: This circuit measures before it ends, so it has no single final state. It was run {{shots}} times, and the classical register read {{readings}} different values.

table.caption: One row per classical register reading: how many runs produced it, and what share of the runs that is.
table.remainder_one: The other reading, on its own

sampling.heading: Shot sampling
sampling.intro: A simulator knows every probability exactly. A real machine is run a number of times and counts what it reads. Draw shots from this state to see the difference.
sampling.enable: Compare a sample with the exact distribution
sampling.summary_one: {{shots}} shot. The largest gap between the sample and the exact distribution is {{gap}}; at this many shots a gap of about {{typical}} is what to expect. Multiply the shots by a hundred and the gap falls by ten.
sampling.summary_other: {{shots}} shots. The largest gap between the sample and the exact distribution is {{gap}}; at this many shots a gap of about {{typical}} is what to expect. Multiply the shots by a hundred and the gap falls by ten.

table.caption: One row per basis state: the exact probability, how many shots landed there, the share that is, and the difference between the two.
